text.p: Germany's third-largest bank said on Tuesday it expected to post a "satisfactory" result for 1996, which would enable it to pay a dividend and to strengthen the bank's reserves.

The bank's chief executive Martin Kohlhaussen said in a newspaper interview last week that Commerzbank did not plan to raise dividend pay-out for 1996 from the level of 13.50 marks ($8.94) paid for 1995 (corrects).
Commerzbank in the first nine months posted a 49 percent rise in pre-tax profits to 1.68 billion marks, a level which already exceeded the full year 1995 pre-tax profit of 1.19 billion marks.
Operating profit before provisions rose 36.9 percent to 1.67 billion marks compared with the year-ago period, below analysts' expectations for a figure of 1.8 billion marks.
